reference.title: Water vapour in the atmosphere of the habitable-zone eight-Earth-mass planet K2-18 b

detections.note: Contested: Bezard et al. 2022, 'Methane as a dominant absorber in the habitable-zone sub-Neptune K2-18 b' (Nature Astronomy 6, 537; doi:10.1038/s41550-022-01678-z) argue the 1.4 micron HST/WFC3 feature 'is most likely due to methane' and is 'not diagnostic of the presence of water vapour' for sub-Neptunes below about 600 K. JWST (Madhusudhan et al. 2023) then detected CH4. (arXiv abstract text contains the macro '\planet\' in place of 'K2-18 b'; it has been replaced in the quote.)
detections.abstract_quote: Here we report the detection of an H2O spectroscopic signature in the atmosphere of K2-18 b -- an eight M⊕ planet in the habitable-zone of an M-dwarf -- with high statistical confidence (ADI = 5.0, ∼3.6σ).

reference.title: Water Vapor and Clouds on the Habitable-zone Sub-Neptune Exoplanet K2-18b

detections.note: Contested: Bezard et al. 2022, 'Methane as a dominant absorber in the habitable-zone sub-Neptune K2-18 b' (Nature Astronomy 6, 537; doi:10.1038/s41550-022-01678-z) argue the 1.4 micron HST/WFC3 feature 'is most likely due to methane' and is 'not diagnostic of the presence of water vapour' for sub-Neptunes below about 600 K. JWST (Madhusudhan et al. 2023) then detected CH4.
detections.abstract_quote: Here, we report the detection of water vapor and the likely presence of liquid and icy water clouds in the atmosphere of the 2.6 R⊕ habitable-zone planet K2-18b.

reference.title: Carbon-bearing Molecules in a Possible Hycean Atmosphere

detections.abstract_quote: The spectrum reveals strong detections of methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2) at 5σ and 3σ confidence, respectively, with high volume mixing ratios of ~1% each in a H2-rich atmosphere.

reference.title: Carbon-bearing Molecules in a Possible Hycean Atmosphere

detections.note: Contested: Schmidt et al. 2025, 'A Comprehensive Reanalysis of K2-18 b's JWST NIRISS+NIRSpec Transmission Spectrum' (AJ 170, 298; doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ae019a) confirm CH4 (about 4 sigma) but 'find no statistically significant or reliable evidence for CO2 or DMS'.
detections.abstract_quote: The spectrum reveals strong detections of methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2) at 5σ and 3σ confidence, respectively, with high volume mixing ratios of ~1% each in a H2-rich atmosphere.

reference.title: Carbon-bearing Molecules in a Possible Hycean Atmosphere

detections.note: Tentative in the original abstract ('potential signs of dimethyl sulfide'), and later contested. Schmidt et al. 2025 (AJ 170, 298; doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ae019a) find 'no statistically significant or reliable evidence for CO2 or DMS'. Luque et al. 2025, 'Insufficient evidence for DMS and DMDS in the atmosphere of K2-18 b. From a joint analysis of JWST NIRISS, NIRSpec, and MIRI observations' (A&A 700, A284; doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202555580) state 'there is no statistical significance for DMS or DMDS in K2-18 b's atmosphere'.
detections.abstract_quote: The spectrum also suggests potential signs of dimethyl sulfide (DMS), which has been predicted to be an observable biomarker in Hycean worlds, motivating considerations of possible biological activity on the planet.
